title: Prudential Standard CPS 230 Operational Risk Management
licence: Commonwealth of Australia, CC BY 4.0 (legislation.gov.au). Text condensed; consult the registered instrument.

companion_guidance: Prudential Practice Guide CPG 230 Operational Risk Management
summary: CPS 230 sets out requirements for APRA-regulated entities to be resilient to operational risks and disruptions. It covers three main pillars: (1) Operational Risk Management (identifying, assessing, controlling, and reporting operational risks); (2) Business Continuity Management (defining critical operations, setting Board-approved tolerance levels for downtime, data loss, and service degradation, and testing credible BCPs); and (3) Service Provider Management (managing material service providers, fourth parties, mandatory agreement clauses, and submitting annual MSP registers to APRA).

clauses.heading: Objectives and key requirements of this Prudential Standard
clauses.text: The aim of this Prudential Standard is to ensure that an APRA-regulated entity is resilient to operational risks and disruptions. An APRA-regulated entity must effectively manage its operational risks, maintain its critical operations through disruptions, and manage the risks arising from service providers. An APRA-regulated entity's approach to operational risk must be appropriate to its size, business mix and complexity.
subclauses: identify, assess and manage its operational risks, with effective internal controls, monitoring and remediation;
be able to continue to deliver its critical operations within tolerance levels through severe disruptions, with a credible business continuity plan (BCP); and
effectively manage the risks associated with service providers, with a comprehensive service provider management policy, formal agreements and robust monitoring.
clauses.notes: Establishes the three pillars: (1) Operational Risk, (2) Business Continuity, (3) Service Provider Management.

clauses.heading: Authority
clauses.text: This Prudential Standard is made under: section 11AF of the Banking Act 1959 (Banking Act); section 32 of the Insurance Act 1973 (Insurance Act); section 230A of the Life Insurance Act 1995 (Life Insurance Act); section 92 of the Private Health Insurance (Prudential Supervision) Act 2015 (PHIPS Act); and section 34C of the Superannuation Industry (Supervision) Act 1993 (SIS Act).
clauses.notes: Covers Banking, General Insurance, Life Insurance, Health Insurance, and Superannuation.

clauses.heading: Scope of Application
clauses.text: This Prudential Standard applies to all APRA-regulated entities defined as: authorised deposit-taking institutions (ADIs), including foreign ADIs, and non-operating holding companies authorised under the Banking Act (authorised banking NOHCs); general insurers, including Category C insurers, non-operating holding companies authorised under the Insurance Act (authorised insurance NOHCs) and parent entities of Level 2 insurance groups; life companies, including friendly societies, eligible foreign life insurance companies (EFLICs) and registered NOHCs; private health insurers registered under the PHIPS Act; and registrable superannuation entity licensees (RSE licensees) under the SIS Act in respect of their business operations.
subclauses: ADIs and authorised banking NOHCs
General insurers, Category C insurers, insurance NOHCs, parent entities of Level 2 insurance groups
Life companies, friendly societies, EFLICs, registered NOHCs
Private health insurers
RSE licensees under the SIS Act
clauses.notes: Comprehensive scope across all prudential sectors.

clauses.heading: Foreign Branches Application
clauses.text: The obligations imposed by this Prudential Standard on, or in relation to, a foreign ADI, a Category C insurer and an EFLIC apply only in relation to the Australian branch operations of that entity.
clauses.notes: Applicable to Australian branch activities.

clauses.heading: Group Compliance
clauses.text: Where an APRA-regulated entity is the Head of a group, it must comply with a requirement of this Prudential Standard: in its capacity as an APRA-regulated entity; by ensuring that the requirement is applied appropriately throughout the group, including in relation to entities that are not APRA-regulated; and on a group basis.
clauses.notes: Requirements flow down throughout corporate groups.

clauses.heading: Commencement Date
clauses.text: This Prudential Standard commences on 1 July 2025 (with amended instrument commencing 1 July 2026). Existing service contracts have transitional arrangements up to contract renewal or 1 July 2026.
clauses.notes: Replaces CPS 231, CPS 232, SPS 231, SPS 232, HPS 231.

clauses.heading: Core Principles of Operational Resilience
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must: effectively manage its operational risks, and set and maintain appropriate standards for conduct and compliance; maintain its critical operations within tolerance levels through severe disruptions; and manage the risks associated with the use of service providers. An APRA-regulated entity must identify, assess and manage operational risks that may result from inadequate or failed internal processes or systems, the actions or inactions of people or external drivers and events. Operational risk is inherent in all products, activities, processes and systems.
subclauses: effectively manage its operational risks, and set and maintain appropriate standards for conduct and compliance;
maintain its critical operations within tolerance levels through severe disruptions; and
manage the risks associated with the use of service providers.
clauses.notes: Foundational mandate covering processes, systems, people, and external events.

clauses.heading: Operational Risk in Risk Management Framework
clauses.text: As part of its risk management framework required under Prudential Standard CPS 220 Risk Management (CPS 220) and Prudential Standard SPS 220 Risk Management (SPS 220), an APRA-regulated entity must develop and maintain: governance arrangements for the oversight of operational risk; an assessment of its operational risk profile, with a defined risk appetite supported by indicators, limits and tolerance levels; internal controls that are designed and operating effectively for the management of operational risks; appropriate monitoring, analysis and reporting of operational risks and escalation processes for operational incidents and events; business continuity plan(s) (BCPs) that set out how the entity would identify, manage and respond to a disruption within tolerance levels and are regularly tested with severe but plausible scenarios; and processes for the management of service provider arrangements.
subclauses: governance arrangements for oversight of operational risk;
assessment of operational risk profile with risk appetite, indicators, limits and tolerance levels;
internal controls designed and operating effectively;
monitoring, analysis and reporting of operational risks and incident escalation;
business continuity plan(s) (BCPs) tested with severe but plausible scenarios; and
processes for the management of service provider arrangements.
clauses.notes: Integrates directly into CPS 220 / SPS 220 overall risk framework.

clauses.heading: Board Ultimate Accountability
clauses.text: The Board of an APRA-regulated entity is ultimately accountable for oversight of an entity's operational risk management. This includes business continuity and the management of service provider arrangements.
clauses.notes: Clear non-delegable Board accountability.

clauses.heading: Mandatory Board Approvals
clauses.text: The Board must: oversee operational risk management and the effectiveness of key internal controls in maintaining the entity's operational risk profile within risk appetite. The Board must be provided with regular updates on the APRA-regulated entity's operational risk profile and ensure senior management takes action as required to address any areas of concern; approve the BCP and tolerance levels for disruptions to critical operations, review the results of testing and oversee the execution of any findings; and approve the service provider management policy, and review risk and performance reporting on material service providers.
subclauses: oversee operational risk management and effectiveness of key internal controls;
approve the BCP and tolerance levels for disruptions to critical operations, review testing results;
approve the service provider management policy and review MSP risk and performance reporting.
clauses.notes: Specific statutory items requiring explicit Board sign-off.

clauses.heading: Full Range of Operational Risks & End-to-End Ownership
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must manage its full range of operational risks, including but not limited to legal risk, regulatory risk, compliance risk, conduct risk, technology risk, data risk and change management risk. Senior management are responsible for operational risk management across the end-to-end process for all business operations.
subclauses: legal risk, regulatory risk, compliance risk
conduct risk
technology risk, data risk
change management risk
clauses.notes: Emphasizes end-to-end process accountability.

clauses.heading: Technology Capability & Intersect with CPS 234
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must maintain appropriate and sound information and information technology (IT) capability to meet its current and projected business requirements and to support its critical operations and risk management. In managing technology risks, an APRA-regulated entity must monitor the age and health of its information assets and meet the requirements for information security in Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security (CPS 234).
clauses.notes: Direct legislative link between CPS 230 and CPS 234.

clauses.heading: Mapping Critical Operations Processes and Resources
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must maintain a comprehensive assessment of its operational risk profile. As part of this, an APRA-regulated entity must: maintain appropriate and effective information systems to monitor operational risk, compile and analyse operational risk data and facilitate reporting to the Board and senior management; identify and document the processes and resources needed to deliver critical operations, including people, technology, information, facilities and service providers, the interdependencies across them, and the associated risks, obligations, key data and controls; and undertake scenario analysis to identify and assess the potential impact of severe operational risk events, test its operational resilience and identify the need for new or amended controls and other mitigation strategies.
subclauses: maintain information systems to monitor operational risk and report to Board/senior management;
identify and document processes and resources needed to deliver critical operations (people, tech, info, facilities, service providers, interdependencies, risks, controls); and
undertake scenario analysis for severe operational risk events to test resilience.
clauses.notes: Requires detailed dependency mapping across technology, people, vendors, and facilities.

clauses.heading: Internal Controls and Remediation
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must design, implement and embed internal controls to mitigate its operational risks in line with its risk appetite and meet its compliance obligations. An APRA-regulated entity must regularly monitor, review and test controls for design and operating effectiveness, the frequency of which must be commensurate with the materiality of the risks being controlled. The results of testing must be reported to senior management and any gaps or deficiencies rectified in a timely manner. An APRA-regulated entity must remediate material weaknesses, control gaps, and failures, addressing root causes.
clauses.notes: Mandates root-cause remediation and tracking open issues in the operational risk profile.

clauses.heading: Incident and Near-Miss Escalation
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must ensure that operational risk incidents and near misses are identified, escalated, recorded and addressed in a timely manner. An APRA-regulated entity must take incidents and near misses into account in its assessment of its operational risk profile and control effectiveness in a timely manner.
clauses.notes: Explicitly requires tracking 'near misses' alongside actual incidents.

clauses.heading: Mandatory 72-Hour APRA Notification for Material Operational Risk Incidents
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must notify APRA as soon as possible, and not later than 72 hours, after becoming aware of an operational risk incident that it determines to be likely to have a material financial impact or a material impact on the ability of the entity to maintain its critical operations.
subclauses: likely to have a material financial impact; or
likely to have a material impact on the ability of the entity to maintain its critical operations.
clauses.notes: Footnote 11: A notification of an information security incident reported under CPS 234 does not need to be separately reported under the notification requirements of this Prudential Standard.

clauses.heading: Business Continuity Core Mandate
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must: define, identify and maintain a register of its critical operations; take reasonable steps to minimise the likelihood and impact of disruptions to its critical operations; maintain a credible BCP that sets out how it would maintain its critical operations within tolerance levels through disruptions, including disaster recovery planning for critical information assets; activate its BCP if needed in the event of a disruption; and return to normal operations promptly after a disruption is over.
subclauses: define, identify and maintain a register of its critical operations;
minimise likelihood and impact of disruptions;
maintain credible BCP with disaster recovery planning for critical information assets;
activate BCP when disrupted; and
return to normal operations promptly.
clauses.notes: Requires DR planning for critical assets and quick recovery.

clauses.heading: Definition and Mandatory Classification of Critical Operations
clauses.text: Critical operations are processes undertaken by an APRA-regulated entity or its service provider which, if disrupted beyond tolerance levels, would have a material adverse impact on its depositors, policyholders, beneficiaries or other customers, or its role in the financial system. An APRA-regulated entity must, at a minimum, classify the following business operations as critical operations, unless it can justify otherwise: for an ADI: payments, deposit-taking and management, custody, settlements and clearing; for an insurer (general, life, private health): claims processing; for an RSE licensee: investment management and fund administration; and for all APRA-regulated entities: customer enquiries and the systems and infrastructure needed to support critical operations.
subclauses: for an ADI (Banking): payments, deposit-taking and management, custody, settlements and clearing;
for an Insurer (General, Life, Health): claims processing;
for an RSE licensee (Superannuation): investment management and fund administration; and
for all APRA-regulated entities: customer enquiries and the systems and infrastructure needed to support critical operations.
clauses.notes: Essential baseline: ADIs must classify payments/deposits/settlements; Insurers must classify claims processing.

clauses.heading: Establishment of Three Tolerance Levels
clauses.text: For each critical operation, an APRA-regulated entity must establish tolerance levels for: the maximum period of time the entity would tolerate a disruption to the operation; the maximum extent of data loss the entity would accept as a result of a disruption; and minimum service levels the entity would maintain while operating under alternative arrangements during a disruption. APRA may require an APRA-regulated entity to review and change its tolerance levels for a critical operation or set tolerance levels where it identifies heightened risk.
subclauses: maximum period of time the entity would tolerate a disruption (downtime / outage duration);
maximum extent of data loss accepted as a result of a disruption (data loss tolerance); and
minimum service levels maintained while operating under alternative arrangements during disruption.
clauses.notes: Every critical operation must have all three tolerances defined and Board-approved.

clauses.heading: Mandatory 24-Hour APRA Notification for Disruption Outside Tolerance
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must notify APRA as soon as possible, and not later than 24 hours after, if it has suffered a disruption to a critical operation outside tolerance. The notification must cover the nature of the disruption, the action taken, the likely impact on the entity's business operations and the timeframe for returning to normal operations.
subclauses: nature of the disruption;
action taken;
likely impact on entity's business operations; and
timeframe for returning to normal operations.
clauses.notes: Most urgent APRA notification timeframe (24 hours). Triggers as soon as an outage exceeds approved tolerance.

clauses.heading: Required Contents of BCP
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity's BCP must include: the register of critical operations and associated tolerance levels; triggers to identify a disruption and prompt activation of the plan, and arrangements to direct resources in the event of activation; actions it would take to maintain its critical operations within tolerance levels through disruptions; an assessment of the execution risks, required resources, preparatory measures, including key internal and external dependencies needed to support the effective implementation of the BCP actions; and a communications strategy to support execution of the plan.
subclauses: register of critical operations and associated tolerance levels;
triggers to identify disruption and prompt activation;
actions to maintain critical operations within tolerance;
assessment of execution risks, dependencies, resources;
communications strategy.
clauses.notes: BCP must be executable and account for external dependencies.

clauses.heading: Systematic BCP Scenario Testing & Annual Exercise
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must have a systematic testing program for its BCP that covers all critical operations and includes an annual business continuity exercise. The program must test the effectiveness of the entity's BCP and its ability to meet tolerance levels in a range of severe but plausible scenarios. The testing program must be tailored to the material risks and include disruptions to services provided by material service providers and scenarios where contingency arrangements are required. Internal audit must periodically review the BCP.
subclauses: annual business continuity exercise covering all critical operations;
range of severe but plausible scenarios including material service provider disruptions;
periodic review and assurance by internal audit.
clauses.notes: APRA may also mandate an APRA-determined scenario for an entity to test.

clauses.heading: Service Provider Management Policy & Fourth Parties
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must maintain a comprehensive service provider management policy. The policy must cover how the entity will identify material service providers and manage service provider arrangements, including the management of material risks associated with the arrangements. The policy must include: the entity's approach to entering into, monitoring, substituting and exiting agreements with material service providers; the entity's approach to managing the risks associated with material service providers; and the entity's approach to managing the risks associated with any fourth parties that material service providers rely on to deliver a critical operation to the APRA-regulated entity.
subclauses: approach to entering into, monitoring, substituting and exiting MSP agreements;
approach to managing risks associated with material service providers; and
approach to managing risks associated with fourth parties (sub-contractors) supporting critical operations.
clauses.notes: Footnote 14: Fourth party is a party that a service provider relies on to deliver services to the regulated entity.

clauses.heading: Definition and Mandatory Classification of Material Service Providers
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must identify and maintain a register of its material service providers and manage the material risks associated with using these providers. Material service providers are those on which the entity relies to undertake a critical operation or that expose it to material operational risk. An APRA-regulated entity must, at a minimum, classify a provider of the following services as a material service provider, unless it can justify otherwise: for an ADI: credit assessment, funding and liquidity management and mortgage brokerage; for an insurer (general, life, private health): underwriting, claims management, insurance brokerage and reinsurance; for an RSE licensee: fund administration, custodial services, investment management and arrangements with promoters and financial planners; and for all APRA-regulated entities: risk management, core technology services and internal audit. The register must be submitted to APRA annually.
subclauses: for an ADI (Banking): credit assessment, funding and liquidity management, and mortgage brokerage;
for an Insurer (General, Life, Health): underwriting, claims management, insurance brokerage, and reinsurance;
for an RSE licensee: fund administration, custodial services, investment management, promoters/planners; and
for all APRA-regulated entities: risk management, core technology services, and internal audit.
clauses.notes: Annual register submission to APRA is mandatory.

clauses.heading: Due Diligence & Mandatory Agreement Terms
clauses.text: Before entering into or materially modifying a material arrangement, an APRA-regulated entity must undertake appropriate due diligence and assess financial and non-financial risks (including geographic concentration). For all material arrangements, an APRA-regulated entity must maintain a formal legally binding agreement. The formal agreement must, at a minimum: specify services covered and service levels; set out rights, responsibilities, asset/data ownership and control, dispute resolution, audit access, liability, and indemnity; include compliance provisions; require notification of material sub-contractors (fourth parties); require service provider liability for sub-contractor failures; include force majeure provisions; and include termination provisions. The formal agreement must also allow APRA access to documentation, data, on-site visits, and ensure the provider agrees not to impede APRA.
subclauses: specify services covered and service levels (SLAs);
set out rights, responsibilities, data ownership and control, audit access, liability, indemnity;
include provisions ensuring ability to meet legal/compliance obligations;
require notification by provider of material sub-contractors (fourth parties);
require liability for sub-contractor failure to remain with the primary service provider;
force majeure and termination provisions;
APRA information access rights, right to conduct on-site visits, and agreement not to impede APRA.
clauses.notes: Mandatory terms that must be present in every material contract.

clauses.heading: Exemptions for Non-Traditional Service Providers
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity need not comply with certain strict contracting requirements (paragraphs 53, 54, 55(d), 59(a), 59(c)) for a material arrangement if: the arrangement is with a service provider that falls within a category listed in the Attachment (Government agencies, Regulators, Central banks, Financial market exchanges, Clearing/settlement facilities, Payment systems/schemes, Financial messaging infrastructures); and the arrangement uses standardised terms or is not documented in a formal agreement.
clauses.notes: Introduced in updated standard F2026L00475 to provide relief for arrangements like RBA, ASX, SWIFT.

clauses.heading: Mandatory 20-Day Agreement Notification to APRA
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must notify APRA as soon as possible and not more than 20 business days after entering into or materially changing an agreement for the provision of a service on which the entity relies to undertake a critical operation.
clauses.notes: Triggered when entering or materially amending an agreement underpinning a critical operation.

clauses.heading: Prior Notification for Material Offshoring Arrangements
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must notify APRA prior to entering into any material offshoring arrangement, or when there is a significant change proposed to the arrangement, including in circumstances where data or personnel relevant to the service being provided will be located offshore.
clauses.notes: Footnote 16: Must notify APRA *prior* to entering arrangement or shifting data/personnel offshore.

clauses.heading: Internal Audit Review of Outsourced Critical Operations
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity's internal audit function must review any proposed material arrangement involving the outsourcing of a critical operation. The internal audit function must regularly report to the Board or Board Audit Committee on compliance of such arrangements with the entity's service provider management policy.
clauses.notes: Requires internal audit involvement prior to executing material outsourcing of critical operations.

clauses.section_name: Attachment - Categories of exempt service providers
clauses.heading: Categories of Exempt Service Providers
clauses.text: Categories of service providers eligible for exemption from certain formal agreement requirements under paragraph 63: Government agencies; Regulators (e.g. APRA, ASIC, ACCC); Central banks (e.g. Reserve Bank of Australia); Financial market exchanges (e.g. ASX); Operators of clearing and settlement facilities (e.g. ASX Clear); Operators of payment systems and schemes (e.g. NPP, EFTPOS, Visa, Mastercard); Financial messaging infrastructures (e.g. SWIFT, SuperStream gateways).
subclauses: Government agencies
Regulators
Central banks
Financial market exchanges
Operators of clearing and settlement facilities
Operators of payment systems and schemes
Financial messaging infrastructures
clauses.notes: Relieves entities from having to negotiate bespoke contracts with monopoly or sovereign infrastructures.
